schedule.title: Accessibility Worst Practices
schedule.desc:
HTML has good accessibility by default, but with a little extra effort, we can make our web content less easily available to everyone. If you'd rather make your content more accessible instead, join us for a look at a few of the worst practices revealed by the 2026 WebAIM Million survey, what to do about them, and better development approaches to accessibility in general.

Learning objectives:

  • Identify some of the most common accessibility problems
  • Understand what options are available in Drupal to address them
  • Understand the WCAG success criteria used to evaluate improvements

schedule.title: Culture mapping the human side of AI — A workshop to meet your people where they are
schedule.desc:
This workshop addresses how leaders can guide colleagues through rapid AI adoption while organizational culture evolves more slowly. Participants use a culture mapping tool to assess where team members stand in their AI adoption journey. The facilitator brings over a decade of consulting and leadership-coaching experience, with certification in the Reinventing Organizations Map (ROM) framework, which evaluates organizational positioning across behavior, culture, systems, and mindset. The ROM tool is licensed under Creative Commons, so it can be used for free beyond the session.

Learning objectives:

  • Assess colleague positions in AI adoption through culture mapping
  • Understand the transition toward agentic organizations across multiple dimensions
  • Develop actionable approaches for meeting people where they are during change

schedule.title: From Ajax API to HTMX: Evolving Drupal Interactions
schedule.desc:
This session explores the evolution of dynamic interactions in Drupal, moving from the traditional Ajax API to the emerging HTMX approach in Drupal 11.3. It begins with an overview of Drupal's Ajax API, its effectiveness, and challenges including complexity, tight JavaScript coupling, and maintenance overhead. The session introduces HTMX and hypermedia-driven interactions, explaining how HTMX aligns with Drupal's core architecture including render arrays, routing, and caching.

Key topics covered include: evolution and limitations of Drupal's Ajax API; core principles of HTMX and hypermedia; mapping HTMX concepts to Drupal architecture; implementing common use cases (dynamic forms, filtering, partial page updates); comparing HTMX and Ajax API regarding developer experience, performance, debugging, and progressive enhancement; incremental adoption strategies in existing Drupal projects; and the current status of HTMX in Drupal core and contribution opportunities.

The session includes real-world examples and a live demonstration showing how HTMX integrates into Drupal's render pipeline.

schedule.title: PHP Packages as Drupal Extensions
schedule.desc: Drupal currently offers three extension types — modules, themes, and profiles — each serving distinct purposes by implementing hooks, event subscribers, and adding services to the container. This session explores an alternative approach: Drupal extensions available immediately upon codebase inclusion via Composer, without requiring installation. This would streamline installation profile customization. Such "package extensions" would operate statelessly, excluding install/update hooks and schema modifications. While achievable through settings.php modifications, this proves inefficient and user-unfriendly at scale. The presenter invites collaborative development of this concept.

schedule.title: Reviewer-Friendly AI: A Practical Drupal Contribution Workshop
schedule.desc:
Bring a Drupal contribution idea — or use one of ours — and work through a practical AI-assisted workflow that turns it into a review-ready contribution designed to earn maintainer trust and accelerate the review process. This workshop is facilitated by Product and Innovation Leads of the Drupal AI Initiative, and is designed to field-test practical patterns that will inform official AI-assisted contribution guidelines.

Prerequisites: Bring a laptop, a contribution idea if you have one, and access to an AI assistant you are comfortable using. Browser-based tools are enough for most lanes. Attendees should be comfortable with basic Drupal concepts, Git, and reading issue queues or project documentation. No prior AI experience is required. Curated issues, templates, checkpoint branches, and a browser-based fallback environment will be provided.

Participants bring a contribution idea — or choose from a curated list — and move through the same structured sequence: understand the issue and prior discussion, write a human task brief with acceptance criteria, add project instructions that constrain the assistant, use AI to draft analysis, docs, tests, or a small code change in reviewable increments, verify the result, disclose AI use clearly, and write a maintainer-friendly handoff comment.

Learning objectives:

  • Turn a Drupal idea or existing issue into a human-authored task brief with context, scope, and acceptance criteria
  • Write project instructions, such as an AGENTS.md, that constrain AI output to Drupal and project-specific expectations
  • Use AI to draft analysis, documentation, tests, or a small code change in reviewable increments instead of dumping a patch
  • Verify AI-generated work for correctness, dependencies, security, licensing, and disclosure
  • Write a maintainer-friendly handoff comment that explains what was done, what was verified, and what feedback is needed

schedule.title: The joy and power of SDC, finally for form inputs
schedule.desc:
We can never get enough of SDC, the front-dev friendly API to implement and share UI components for Drupal. This session covers the biggest improvement since the introduction of the API: soon it will be possible to implement form elements directly with SDC, using only UI logic and front-end technologies, without touching backend APIs.

The introduction of SDC to Core in 2023 had a significant impact on the Drupal ecosystem, starting a movement to embrace design system methodology, helping front-end designers implement ambitious shareable designs, and bringing display building back to the forefront. However, UI components related to form inputs — date pickers, interactive data tables, file uploaders, sliders, toggles, draggable tree views — can't yet be implemented as SDC and are still managed the old way, with abstruse PHP classes.

Support for form elements in SDC is landing in 2026. Full component libraries will be packageable as Drupal themes and shared between projects, and front-end developers will finally get full ownership of design implementations. It will also be an opportunity to clean up large parts of the rendering pipeline by finalizing the split between UI logic and business logic. The session explores how to use these new UI components programmatically in front-end and back-end development, with demos of their use from the Admin UI, leveraging them as Field Widgets to build an Entity Form Display.

schedule.title: Why Your AI Agent Hallucinates: Engineering Lessons From a Production Workflow Builder in Drupal
schedule.desc: LLMs are now table stakes in Drupal. Modules like AI, ECA, and a growing set of agentic tools make it trivial to wire a model into a site. What's not trivial is making that integration trustworthy enough to put in front of a real editor or site builder. Over the last several months, building FlowDrop's chat-based workflow editor, the speaker collected a set of failure modes that recur across every LLM-driven Drupal feature: hallucinated field names, half-applied state changes, prompt-injection through user content, runaway token costs as state grows, and the "what ID did you just create?" round-trip problem. This session is the post-mortem: the engineering log of what changed, why each change mattered, and how each pattern generalises beyond FlowDrop, with every claim backed by code and data shown on screen.

schedule.title: Getting the most out of GitLab Issue Queues
schedule.desc:
If you work with Drupal issue queues, you may have noticed a recent change.

We've been using GitLab for merge requests since 2021, but now issue queues are migrating to GitLab.

Hundreds of projects have already moved over to the new GitLab issue queues, with all 50,000+ projects on Drupal.org set to follow over the coming months (years?).

It should result in a more integrated experience, but it will also bring new ways of working, and new challenges.

Join us and review some best practices being adopted by the community, and look at some tips to help ease the changeover.

This is intended to be an open discussion, and everyone is welcome to share their favourite GitLab tips.

schedule.title: Context Control Center: Bringing AI Context Natively to Drupal CMS
schedule.desc:
Your AI features are only as good as the knowledge behind them. Context Control Center is how Drupal CMS keeps that knowledge structured, scoped, and ready for every agent and request. Whether powering help desks, personalized experiences, automated emails, or site search, the same governed library feeds them all.

AI in Drupal only looks "smart" when the model knows your organization's facts, policies, and constraints. That knowledge typically lives in Slack threads, PDFs, and ad-hoc prompts, so outputs can drift and contradict each other. The hard problem is not picking an AI model; it is keeping truth structured, current, and attached to the right workflow.

Context Control Center (CCC) is the native context layer in Drupal CMS: a place to author, review, translate, and reuse context items for AI features and agents. Instead of everyone pasting their own detailed prompt, Drupal assembles the right context from one governed library per agent and request. Topics covered include context scopes (language, site section, use case), remote context sources, and best practices for structuring and maintaining context.

schedule.title: Drupal as an MCP Server: Making Your CMS a First-Class Citizen in the Agentic Web
schedule.desc:
AI agents are becoming the new users of the web, and most CMSes are invisible to them. This session shows how to expose Drupal as an MCP server, turning content infrastructure into something AI agents can reason about, query, and act on, in production.

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is rapidly becoming the standard interface layer between AI agents and external systems — how tools like Claude, Cursor, and autonomous coding agents connect to APIs, databases, and services in a structured, safe, and composable way. Most Drupal sites are built for human browsers, but the next wave of users will be AI agents: automated pipelines, LLM-powered assistants, and agentic workflows that need to read, create, and manage structured content. Drupal's entity system, typed fields, and REST/JSON:API layers make it uniquely well-suited to serve this role, but only if bridged deliberately.

The session walks through the architecture and implementation of a Drupal MCP server: exposing content types, taxonomy, media, and workflows as MCP tools and resources that AI agents can discover and use, covering protocol fundamentals, mapping Drupal's data model onto MCP primitives, authentication and permission scoping, and production challenges.

schedule.title: Drupal Association Public Board Meeting
Drupal in a Days: One Year Later
schedule.desc:
Drupal in a Days: One Year Later offers insights from organizers, teachers, and initiative members sharing success stories from events held globally since DrupalCon Vienna 2025. The session features a short introduction followed by a panel discussion where participants can hear testimonies, view pictures and statistics, and ask questions about organizing their own Drupal in a Day event.

The program covers why to organize a Drupal in a Day, where to start, becoming a teacher, and future directions. Learning objectives include understanding the project's current state, connecting with initiative actors, recognizing the concept's potential, and realizing that materials are available for anyone to organize an edition.

schedule.title: Encoding Expertise: How UX Research Powers Human-First AI
schedule.desc:
UX research practices matter more than ever in the age of AI slop. AI content tools produce generic output because nobody has told them what "good" means for your organization, and getting at that is exactly what UX researchers are trained to do. Interviews, comparative evaluation, rubric design: existing toolkits, applied to a new and urgent problem. The organizations that get this right will outcompete the ones still generating slop.

Prerequisites: No technical prerequisites. Attendees will get the most value if they work with web content in some capacity: content strategists, UX researchers, marketers, editorial leads, or Drupal site owners thinking about AI content tools. Basic experience with brand writing guidelines, editorial style guides, or content strategy work is helpful but not required.

The session outline covers the problem (the gap between documented and tacit quality standards), the method (UX research approaches), and the payoff (aligned teams and human-first AI integration with Drupal's Context Control Center and Canvas AI).

schedule.title: Mentor Orientation - Tuesday
One Portal, 16 Markets: How Sharp Built a Pan-European Partner Ecosystem on Drupal
schedule.desc:
Sharp Electronics operates a Drupal-powered partner portal serving 6,000 Sharp dealer users across 1,200+ dealerships in 16 European markets, giving them access to pricing, product knowledge, and marketing assets.

Business problem: fragmented tools (emails, spreadsheets, legacy on-premise systems) created friction for dealer relationships and obscured deal pipeline visibility.

Solution components:

  • Dealer portal with self-service pricing requests, real-time status tracking, team access management, product discovery, co-branded asset downloads, and a searchable knowledge base covering 28,000+ products
  • Internal knowledge hub replacing a legacy system with 3,000+ structured, searchable articles

Key topics covered:

  • B2B partner portal capabilities using Drupal
  • Role-based access and structured content workflows for diverse user groups
  • Legacy system migration to Drupal
  • Multi-market, multi-language deployment complexity management
  • Enterprise business case framework for Drupal adoption

Prerequisites: No technical background required; basic CMS familiarity helpful.

Target audience: Digital leaders, product owners, IT decision-makers at mid-to-large organizations; Drupal practitioners.

schedule.title: When the roadmap is a battleground: building a shared Drupal platform for government
schedule.desc:
Come for the architecture, stay for the honest story. This session takes you inside the Government Drupal Platform, the recipe-driven foundation behind Dutch central government websites. What choices did we make, and would we make them again? Where does technical architecture meet the people who have to live with it?

Everyone building a shared Drupal platform for government hits the same wall: stakeholders think their case is the exception, the roadmap is a battleground, and every release that makes one agency happy can break something for another.

DICTU's Government Drupal Platform provisions fully accessible, Rijksoverheid-branded government websites in under 10 minutes using 30+ recipes, aligned with Drupal CMS. Winner of the Drupal Splash Awards Government category 2025, and one year in production by the time we take this stage.

We will show how we keep recipes composable and conflict-free, how CI/CD makes 10-minute provisioning possible, and how technical decisions ripple through to the editors who use them. We'll share what reluctant users taught us, how early adopters became co-creators, and what we learned from those who walked away. We are releasing new recipes for this event, and our design system is already public.

Learning objectives:

  • Recipe-driven architecture at scale in a production government environment with 30+ composable, conflict-free recipes
  • A technology-agnostic design system connecting a national design system to Drupal via a Figma-to-code pipeline
  • CI/CD automation enabling 10-minute site provisioning
  • How technical decisions shape editor and end-user experience
  • Managing shared platforms when adoption isn't universal
  • Concrete open-source assets: recipes and design system available for reuse

schedule.title: Coffee Break 2, Tuesday
Agentic Debugging: Teaching AI to Step Through Your Code
schedule.desc:
Your AI can read every line of your code — but it has never watched it run. Until now. This session addresses how AI assistants remain blind to runtime state when debugging, establishing an architecture that grants them visibility through breakpoints, call stacks, variables, and expression evaluation via open protocols.

Session outline:

  • The problem: AI assistants read code but cannot observe runtime state; they guess at bugs rather than proving them
  • Architecture deep-dive: a VS Code LM Tools mode (16 tools) and an MCP server mode (20 tools over stdio/Streamable HTTP) sharing one backend-agnostic tool layer
  • Strict debug flow & tool schema: a custom debug agent with state-machine transitions (launch → listen → connect → pause → inspect → step → terminate)
  • Multi-language & CLI bridge: extension to Node.js, Python, and Go via a DebugBackend interface abstraction
  • Agent skills, Playwright integration & MCP resources exposing breakpoints, call stacks, and session state
  • Live demo: an agent autonomously reproduces a bug, sets strategic breakpoints, inspects runtime state, and reports root cause

Prerequisites: familiarity with VS Code debugging (breakpoints, call stack panel, variables view); basic understanding of LLMs/AI agents and tools like Copilot and Cursor. No specific language expertise required.

Target audience: Developers.

schedule.title: AI-Assisted Contrib Module Maintenance
schedule.desc:
Maintaining a Drupal module often means juggling triage, reviews, contributor guidance, and releases — all within an ever-growing issue queue. In this session, we'll explore how coding agents with deterministic code can act as helper tools, reducing this burden while improving quality and consistency. We'll showcase an open source tool already used in practice to automate tasks like duplicate detection, pre-reviewing code, effort estimation, and suggesting next steps before work even begins.

The session expands into a broader vision where these tools go beyond triage: summarizing complex issue threads, proposing reproduction steps, analyzing patch impact, and identifying missing tests or potential BC breaks. As part of CI, functional testing is automatically recorded as video, giving maintainers and contributors a clear, visual way to verify changes after code is pushed.

By the end of this session, you'll see how open source AI tooling and coding agents can help, but not replace, maintainers.

Learning objectives:

  • Understand how coding agents can support Drupal maintenance workflows
  • Learn how to automate issue triage, code review, and prioritization tasks
  • Explore practical use cases for improving issue queue quality and contributor experience
  • Discover how automated functional testing videos can improve validation and collaboration

schedule.title: Beyond content staging: where Drupal Workspaces is heading
schedule.desc:
Workspaces functionality extends beyond content staging to encompass governed change across content, config, and AI-assisted workflows. The session progresses from foundational content staging needs through Workspaces' core stability, integration with Content Moderation, the Workspaces Extra module's experimental features (configuration staging, workspace previews, revert options), and AI governance considerations where changes should not go directly to live unless intended.

Learning objectives:

  • Understand the current Workspaces implementation in core
  • Identify contrib extensions, particularly Workspaces Extra
  • Recognize config staging significance for AI governance
  • Evaluate human-in-the-loop approaches for AI-driven changes
  • Distinguish between ready-now versus evolving components

Prerequisites: familiarity with Drupal core concepts (entities, configuration, editorial workflows), Content Moderation, publishing workflows, and general awareness of AI tooling.

Target audience: Drupal developers, technical leads, solution architects, and experienced site builders working on enterprise platforms with complex publishing needs or evaluating Workspaces and related modules.

schedule.title: Building Production-Ready AI Applications Using Curated Drupal Recipes
schedule.desc:
Move your Drupal projects from AI experimentation to enterprise-ready implementation. This workshop provides hands-on experience deploying secure, agentic AI features and automated content workflows using curated, official tools.

Outline:

  • Foundation: Drupal CMS setup, AI providers, context management
  • Governance: Guardrails (PII protection), Observability, debugging tools
  • Assistants: AI Content Reviews, QA automation, native AI tools
  • Search: RAG-powered semantic search
  • MCP: bi-directional communication with external agents

Learning objectives:

  • Deploy secure AI foundations with providers, context management, Guardrails, and Observability
  • Configure AI Content Reviews and editorial assistants for QA automation without custom code
  • Implement semantic search and configure Drupal as a secure MCP server

Target audience: Site builders, developers, and digital strategists implementing AI features in Drupal projects.

Prerequisites: familiarity with Drupal site building (content types, fields) and basic DDEV/Composer usage; no programming experience required.

schedule.title: Drupal CMS spotlights
schedule.desc:
Lightning talks from Drupal CMS leads — short deep-dives into specific areas of Drupal CMS.

Prerequisites: a rough idea of Drupal CMS.

Target audience: varied, depending on the lightning talk.

schedule.title: First-Time Contributor Workshop - Tuesday
From Vendor Lock-In to Digital Sovereignty: A Practical Roadmap for Governments & EU Institutions
schedule.desc:
Digital sovereignty is no longer a policy goal — it's a technical challenge. Many government and EU platforms remain dependent on external vendors and closed systems. This session provides a roadmap for transitioning to control through Drupal's open, modular architecture and open standards commitment, enabling public organizations to build transparent, interoperable platforms under their control while reducing lock-in and ensuring sustainability.

The session addresses digital sovereignty as a strategic priority for governments and EU institutions, breaking it into actionable layers: dependency assessment, architecture design, implementation strategy, and long-term governance. Key topics include identifying and reducing vendor lock-in in public-sector systems, designing open API-first architectures with Drupal, infrastructure and hosting considerations in a European context, migration strategies from proprietary or SaaS platforms, and governance models that prevent future lock-in.

Learning objectives:

  • Understand what digital sovereignty means in practical, technical terms
  • Identify risks and signs of vendor lock-in in existing systems
  • Learn a step-by-step roadmap to design sovereign digital platforms
  • Apply Drupal's architecture to support open standards and interoperability
  • Evaluate trade-offs between SaaS, cloud, and open-source approaches

schedule.title: Beyond the CMS: Drupal as the Backbone of an Open Health Platform
schedule.desc:
A real-world case study of Drupal used not as a traditional CMS, but as a headless governance and integration layer inside an open digital health platform: the Plataforma Oberta de Salut de Catalunya, where Drupal 11 is used as a headless backend for catalog management, APIs, taxonomy, governance and lifecycle orchestration of digital health assets. The platform integrates React microfrontends, identity and access management, BPMN workflows, Kafka event processing, clinical and citizen channels, Backstage developer tooling, and OpenSearch/OpenTelemetry observability.

The challenge addressed is health information fragmentation across disconnected systems. The solution aims for an open, modular and interoperable public digital foundation supporting integrated care and digital sovereignty through open-source technologies and standards.

Learning objectives: understand how Drupal functions as a headless platform backend; learn responsibility separation between Drupal, frontends, workflows, and event services; see ecosystem integrations; identify reusable patterns for governed digital marketplaces; explore how open standards support interoperability and sustainability.

Prerequisites: basic understanding of Drupal and modern web architectures will help, especially concepts such as headless CMS, APIs and frontend/backend separation. No healthcare background is required.

Target audience: Drupal architects, developers, technical leads; digital platform teams; public sector/government teams; innovation and product owners.

schedule.title: Help shape Drupal’s story: A global marketing call to action
schedule.desc:
What if Drupal marketed itself as powerfully as it's built? Join us to help shape the future of Drupal's global story.

Drupal is entering a new era of marketing momentum following increased visibility through external events, webinars, and award wins. Presenters will discuss how community alignment around shared messaging amplifies reach, the Drupal Association's coordinated marketing efforts in new areas, why marketing is becoming one of the most accessible and high-impact ways to contribute, and practical opportunities for individuals and organizations to raise their profile.

Learning objectives:

  • Understand the goals and structure of Drupal's global marketing initiative
  • Learn from recent efforts including Drupal AI marketing campaigns
  • Identify contribution opportunities to shared marketing efforts
  • Gain practical ways to support Drupal's positioning

schedule.title: How Drupal drives Pinball Machines
schedule.desc:
The session explores the intersection of Drupal and the open source pinball community. Markus Kalkbrenner established ppuc.org (Pinball Power-Up Community) five years ago to develop open source hardware and software for preserving and enhancing vintage pinball machines, as well as enabling homebrew pinball machine construction.

Drupal serves as a component within this ecosystem, particularly for managing game, hardware, and effect configurations, and facilitating collaboration. Specific Drupal contrib modules highlighted include Default Content Deploy for sharing content across installations and AI tools for extracting information from historical manuals.

The session balances Drupal-specific content with broader discussion of open source developments in the pinball community and pinball machine fundamentals.

Learning objectives: understanding how Drupal functions as an embedded tool within larger ecosystems; learning pinball machine basics and the role of open source software and hardware in the pinball community.

schedule.title: You can (and should!) build a site template
schedule.desc:
Site templates are significant in expanding Drupal's reach by delivering functional and beautiful starter sites, and the community is essential for creating them.

The session covers two primary approaches: the expedited method, enabling site builders to leverage Drupal CMS for delivering excellent templates with minimal coding, and the comprehensive method, for developers prioritizing organized recipes, clean architecture, thorough testing, and reliability.

Through practical examples and live demonstrations of the recipe stack, attendees gain actionable knowledge and confidence to architect templates meeting current organizational requirements while remaining flexible for future needs.

Learning objectives:

  • Create a site template
  • Publish a site template
  • Build a library of recipes and tools for rapidly constructing new templates

Prerequisites: basic Drupal site building skills.

Target audience: site builders interested in publishing site templates.

schedule.title: Your Dashboard Is Lying: Goodhart's Law and the Metrics Crisis in AI-Era Drupal Delivery
schedule.desc:
Your delivery metrics have never looked better. Your AI tools are closing tickets, boosting velocity, and painting every dashboard green. So why did the client just escalate?

The session explores Goodhart's Law — "when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure" — and its application to Drupal agency delivery. It examines four metrics (velocity, ticket resolution time, SLA response rate, sprint burndown) showing how each becomes vulnerable to gaming, particularly with AI acceleration. The talk introduces measurement hygiene frameworks distinguishing vanity metrics from genuine health signals, including leading indicators like decision-log freshness and risk-to-mitigation ratio.

Prerequisites: project management or delivery experience in Drupal agency/client-services contexts; practical familiarity with velocity, burndown, and SLAs; no economics background required.

Target audience: agency owners, project managers, account managers, Scrum masters, Agile coaches, operations leads.

schedule.title: A developer is more than their code: growing the seniors of 2031
schedule.desc:
AI can write your code. But can it make you a better developer? The session explores how artificial intelligence changes developer education, drawing on junior developer mentorship at Agiledrop, a 70+ engineer organization.

The presenter argues that fundamental developer competencies — debugging, collaboration, problem-solving, and ownership — cannot be learned through AI tools alone. The session documents a structured 1–3 month onboarding approach and warns that juniors who leaned too hard on AI tools learned less deeply. It connects junior developer growth directly to open-source community sustainability, particularly for Drupal's future.

Learning objectives:

  • Understand why communication, problem-solving, and teamwork cannot develop through AI alone
  • Learn a tested onboarding methodology from a 70+ person engineering company
  • Recognize signs junior developers over-rely on AI in ways that impede growth
  • Connect mentorship to open-source community health

Prerequisites: no technical knowledge required.

schedule.title: Can AI Fix the Web? The Promises and Perils of "Automated" Accessibility
schedule.desc:
We are entering a dangerous new era of web development where teams are asking Generative AI to "fix my WCAG errors." On the surface, it sounds like a utopia: pass your broken DOM to a large language model and get a perfectly accessible component returned in seconds. However, AI operates on statistical probability, not human empathy. Relying on AI to automatically patch accessibility often produces hallucinated ARIA labels, nonsensical focus trapping, and fundamentally broken screen-reader experiences that technically pass automated audits but fail actual users.

This session explores the intersection of Generative AI and web accessibility, where AI fails spectacularly at inclusive design, and how engineering teams can pragmatically use AI as an assistive testing and ideation tool rather than an automated fix. As developers, we cannot outsource human empathy to an algorithm.

Learning objectives:

  • Understand why LLMs fail at complex inclusive design and how to spot "fake" accessibility fixes in AI-generated code
  • Learn how to write specific, context-aware prompts that force AI to act as a rigorous accessibility auditor rather than an automated code generator
  • Grasp the ethical implications of outsourcing digital inclusion to algorithms, and establish team guardrails for AI use in front-end development

Prerequisites: basic understanding of web accessibility principles (WCAG, ARIA, semantic HTML); familiarity with using AI coding assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot).

schedule.title: Drupal CMS by design: How continuous UX research is building a product you can depend on
schedule.desc:
Drupal CMS development follows research, evidence, and a relentless focus on what people actually need. Emma Horrell, UX Research Lead, discusses the evidence-led roadmap integrating insights from Drupal Marketplace, the AI Initiative, and ECA next generation. Topics covered include site templates, onboarding, content and editorial workflows, migration, and integrations.

Learning objectives:

  • Understand feature rationale connected to audience needs
  • Engage directly with UX research leadership
  • Appreciate the evidence-led development process
  • Contribute to Drupal CMS's future direction

Target audience: existing Drupal CMS users, prospective users, site builders, content creators, developers, and contributors with interest in UX research and product development.

schedule.title: From Legacy Chaos to Drupal CMS: AI-Assisted Content Modeling & Migration
schedule.desc:
This session examines how AI supports site builders and product teams in making faster, more confident decisions during content migration projects, focusing on understanding legacy content rather than simply moving data.

Key topics covered:

  • Content discovery using AI to analyze legacy HTML and detect repeatable structures
  • The AI Content Migrate module's role in proposing Drupal content types and fields
  • Mapping fields and extracting structured data using generated selectors
  • Preparing migration configurations aligned with modern Drupal CMS best practices
  • Iterative workflows with safer rollbacks

Learning objectives:

  • Apply AI to content discovery by analyzing legacy HTML structures
  • Bridge gaps between unstructured legacy content and Drupal CMS architectures
  • Critically evaluate AI-generated suggestions while maintaining human judgment
  • Implement efficient, iterative content modeling workflows

Prerequisites: basic understanding of Drupal's content architecture, familiarity with content migration concepts, and general awareness of how LLMs function.

schedule.title: Gander in the Wild: How We Built a Performance Safety Net into Our CI/CD Pipeline
schedule.desc:
Performance regressions are silent killers — they sneak in one commit at a time, and by the time someone notices, the debt is enormous. Gander, included in Drupal core since version 10.2, enables catching these issues early during merge requests.

This session demonstrates integrating Gander's performance assertions into CI/CD pipelines to fail builds when budgets are exceeded, requiring no dedicated infrastructure. Attendees receive configuration templates and implementation checklists.

Outline:

  • The "shift left" case — why retroactive tools like Lighthouse prove insufficient during development
  • Gander's assertion model — measured metrics, PHPUnit functional test extensions, and zero-infrastructure pass/fail methodology
  • From local to pipeline — writing performance tests, defining budgets by content type and user role, configuring CI runners, interpreting failed builds
  • Lessons learned — iterating budgets, managing flaky CI metrics, building team engagement
  • Going further — OpenTelemetry integration, Grafana monitoring, Grafana Tempo distributed tracing roadmap

Learning objectives: understand proactive performance testing advantages over retroactive tools; write Gander assertions in PHPUnit tests with meaningful budgets; configure CI/CD pipelines to enforce performance thresholds.

Prerequisites: PHPUnit test proficiency and basic CI/CD pipeline understanding.

schedule.title: Take Back Your Autonomy
schedule.desc:
The session explores maintaining developer control in AI-accelerated workflows: we are no longer just handing over repetitive tasks — we are also delegating understanding.

It examines hidden trade-offs of AI-assisted coding and loss of architectural awareness, challenges the sufficiency of "it works" as a standard, and provides practical strategies for validating AI-generated code and maintaining accountability, emphasizing intentional development over speed-focused practices.

Learning objectives:

  • Understand trade-offs of heavy AI reliance
  • Recognize loss of architectural awareness
  • Learn code validation techniques
  • Build accountability habits
  • Use AI tools critically while retaining autonomy

Prerequisites: basic familiarity with modern development workflows and interest in AI tools like Claude or Cursor; no advanced AI knowledge required.

Target audience: mid-level and senior PHP/Drupal developers using AI tools; team leads and architects seeking technical ownership alongside AI productivity gains.

schedule.title: Advanced Site Building with Drupal Canvas
schedule.desc:
Learn how Drupal Canvas gives even more power to Drupal Site Builders!

Enabling ambitious site builders has always been a superpower of Drupal and the introduction of Drupal Canvas has taken this to another level. Attendees will learn how to combine the power of Canvas with existing core modules like Views and popular contrib modules, all without writing any code!

We will demonstrate how to build a demo site that leverages Drupal's robust information architecture capabilities alongside the streamlined user experience offered by Drupal Canvas.

Attendees will learn how to:

  • Create dynamic landing pages
  • Use Canvas templates to format all your structured content (nodes, terms, users, etc.)
  • Link field data inside templates to SDC and Code Component properties
  • Display related content on Canvas templates, for example displaying content linked by entity reference fields or the author
  • Use Canvas to control how the related content is displayed
  • Manage permissions to tailor the user experience of Canvas for different user groups
  • Build Views to showcase related content and author details inside Canvas templates
  • Translate Canvas Pages and templates for multi-lingual support

Prerequisite: A basic understanding of Drupal concepts and site building is recommended.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: AI-assisted site migration to Drupal Canvas: a real-world case study
schedule.desc:
AI coding agents are changing how we build software, but can they migrate a real production site to Drupal Canvas? We put it to the test on a live project and share what worked, what didn't, and what the numbers actually say.

Migrating an existing site to Drupal Canvas is a significant undertaking. This session shares a real-world case study of migrating a live site to a Drupal Canvas installation using decoupled rendering, with an AI coding agent driving a large portion of the work, including:

  • The starting point: the legacy site, its content model, and the migration goals
  • Why Drupal Canvas and why decoupled: the architectural decisions behind the project
  • AI driven: how the task was planned to be AI agent led
  • What worked well: tasks where the AI agent was genuinely productive
  • What needs improvement: pitfalls, dead ends, and places where human intervention was required
  • Measuring efficiency: KPIs, time saved (or not), and honest numbers from the project

Prerequisites: Familiarity with Drupal site building, Drupal Canvas and content modelling. Basic awareness of decoupled Drupal architectures and AI coding agents is helpful but not required.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: AI-Augmented Accessibility: From Automated Alt-Text to Governance Gates
schedule.desc:
Stop reacting to accessibility errors and start automating inclusive governance. Learn how to use AI to find accessibility errors earlier and fix them faster. We'll bridge the gaps between AI, code, and humans with clear guidance for everyone.

Accessibility is often the last gate in a project. Like many bugs the longer they wait, the more difficult they are to fix. Learn how we can "shift left" by using AI not just to find errors, but to build better systems. This session provides a practical roadmap for integrating AI into the full Drupal lifecycle:

  • Content: Automating descriptive alt-text & transcripts using Drupal AI Core
  • Infrastructure: Using LLMs to architect & configure CI/CD accessibility gates (Axe-core/Playwright)
  • Triage: Leveraging GitHub's AI-powered accessibility tools to turn scans into Pull Requests
  • Governance: Implementing ACCESSIBILITY.md or Claude skills to produce better results
  • Hierarchy of Truth: Adding AI roles to that of other automated tools & humans—why the user remains the ultimate source of truth

Mike will also be tying this into the book he recently co-authored: Digital Accessibility Ethics: Disability Inclusion in All Things Tech.

Prerequisite: Familiarity with accessibility basics is useful; this is not an introductory session.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: Hidden Skills of Development: Practical Building Blocks for Team Health
schedule.desc:
Start debugging your culture alongside your code. Learn the hidden communication frameworks supporting high-performance teamwork. This session looks into the hidden skills that help prevent burnout, support psychological safety, and provide you the building blocks towards a culture where every developer can learn, contribute and thrive.

Teams do not succeed on technical skill alone. They also need trust, clear communication, room to ask questions, and a culture where people can admit uncertainty before problems grow. In this session, we demonstrate the hidden skills behind healthier teamwork with practical everyday examples. We focus on identifying psychological safety needs and personal differences while collaborating. We help people increase their team's health and prevent burnout by highlighting how communication frameworks can help with imposter syndrome and streamline decision making.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: Mentor Orientation - Wednesday
Nobody Asked for a CMS: From Content Management to Answer Delivery in the Age of AI
schedule.desc:
Nobody asked for a CMS. Organisations needed to share knowledge; users needed answers they could trust. Yet many digital projects still revolve around the CMS itself: content types, workflows, menus, permissions and publishing models while users remain stuck between search results, intranets, PDFs and support channels.

This session uses Helsinki Uni Help, a Finnish university/public-service AI search project, as the main proof point for a wider shift: content management is moving from page publishing toward governed knowledge flow. It will show how Drupal can act as the trusted content and governance layer behind an AI answer experience: structured source material, editorial ownership, multilingual content, integrations, retrieval, citations and feedback loops.

The session will also briefly contrast this with an Astro + LLM publishing experiment, where the traditional CMS UI is no longer the primary editing interface. The point is not that CMSs are dying. The point is that AI changes what the CMS is for.

Attendees will leave with a practical model for deciding when Drupal should be the editing interface, when it should be the content infrastructure, and how to think about AI, search and content governance beyond "which CMS should we use?"

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: Rebuilding the LMS Mid-Flight: A Drupal Success Story with AFT and AFL-CIO
schedule.desc:
Rebuilding a live LMS is risky. Rebuilding it while it powers mission-critical training for organizations like the American Federation of Teachers and the AFL-CIO is even harder. This session takes you through that journey—from growing pains and technical debt to a fully reimagined Drupal-native solution—sharing the lessons learned along the way.

What happens when your LMS outgrows its foundation? This session tells the story of how a long-running e-learning platform for the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), later adopted by the AFL-CIO, evolved from a heavily customized Opigno-based solution into a fully Drupal-native LMS.

Originally launched in 2018 by Tag1 Consulting, the platform scaled across multiple high-impact education sites. However, limitations in flexibility, maintainability, and community responsiveness led the team to rethink the architecture. Starting in 2022, the project underwent a major transformation: key modules were forked, legacy constraints removed, and new foundations built using Drupal core APIs.

We'll walk through the journey from technical debt to innovation, including the first clean alpha release in 2024, the official Drupal LMS project launch in 2025, and the successful production migration in early 2026.

Experience Level: Anyone

schedule.title: Shipping products with confidence: how we rebuilt our testing tools for velocity
schedule.desc:
Confidence in shipping a Drupal-based product shouldn't require 6 days of GitHub runner time with flaky tests across 500+ jobs. This session covers the migration from Behat and PHPUnit to custom tooling built on Playwright to restore testing velocity and reliability.

Using the testing pyramid framework, the presentation audits test suites to evaluate what is tested, at what cost, and whether confidence justifies the investment. Three core components are introduced:

  • QA API/Test Control Interface (TCI): A hidden, environment-gated HTTP API within Drupal providing attribute-driven PHP operations. Modules declare QA operations published as OpenAPI specs, decoupling test data setup from test runners.
  • Playwright harness: Enables first-class trace files, automatic retries, and scalable parallel execution with improved debugging capabilities.
  • Human-readable specs: Cucumber-based UI tests readable by non-engineers and AI-friendly; Markdown-based GraphQL specs embedding queries, variables, and expectations as dual documentation.

Prerequisites: Basic programming understanding and familiarity with PHP testing.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: Clean Code in the Age of AI: Writing for Humans When Machines Write the Code
schedule.desc:
When AI writes the code, clean code becomes the developer's most important job.

AI tools can generate working code faster than ever—but working code is no longer always the hard part. The real challenge is reading, reviewing, and maintaining code that humans can understand and trust.

In this session, we'll revisit the principles of clean code through a modern lens: a world where developers increasingly review AI-generated code instead of writing every line by hand. We'll explore what "clean code" means when the author might be a machine, and why readability, intent, and consistency matter more than ever.

Using Drupal backend examples, we'll look at common issues introduced by AI-assisted development and how to refactor them into code that communicates clearly. The focus is not on style rules, but on writing code that makes reviews faster, safer, and more effective.

Prerequisites: Basic Drupal development knowledge; experience reading and reviewing code; some exposure to AI coding tools is helpful but not required.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: Democratizing Enterprise Applications: Positioning Drupal as a Strategic Low-Code Framework
schedule.desc:
Why pay rent for a "black-box" solution when you can own the foundation? Discover how to transform Drupal from a CMS into a sovereign Low-Code powerhouse that rivals proprietary enterprise systems while maintaining complete data ownership.

Drupal has evolved beyond its "just a CMS" reputation into a strategic Low-Code framework capable of replacing complex proprietary business applications. This session demonstrates building sovereign, cost-effective alternatives to proprietary tools using Drupal's open source ecosystem.

The presentation explores three core pillars transforming Drupal into a "digital factory":

  • Webform: Builder for complex, accessible multi-step forms with conditional logic—entirely without code
  • ECA: Visual process automation using the BPMN standard for Event-Condition-Action workflows
  • Drupal AI: Native AI integration for intelligent workflows and transaction processing

Head-to-head comparison with proprietary market leaders, analyzing ROI of zero license fees versus total cost of ownership and strategic value of open source ownership.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: Drupal CMS, site templates and beyond
schedule.desc:
Drupal CMS continues to evolve, with version 2 including full support for Drupal Canvas, as well as a library of site templates providing feature-rich and uniquely designed starting points for Drupal sites.

Six months later, the session will evaluate the real-world impact of site templates, Canvas and CMS in general on the Drupal ecosystem. Coverage includes how Drupal CMS can help on existing websites, as well as feedback from real life use so far.

Missing features include multilingual support for Canvas and site templates, along with other items. The roadmap for the next 1-2 years will be discussed, covering achievements, ongoing work, and areas needing contributor help.

  • Canvas usage and capabilities
  • Currently developed features and areas
  • Future version plans
  • Contributor opportunities
  • Drupal CMS 2.0 development highlights and lessons learned

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: Drupal.org Engineering Panel
Inside the Pyramid - A path to faster, clearer Drupal testing
schedule.desc:
Your Drupal test suite is slow and it doesn't have to be. The test pyramid has been a cornerstone of software quality for decades, yet Drupal core has no formal guidelines instructing contributors how to write automated tests. This session will cover both the current state – discussing techniques to write faster tests – and how to change Drupal to make these improvements structural.

Drupal's automated test suite is a huge achievement – literally – but it is slow, and one of the reasons is structural: there are no official guidelines prescribing which test type to use for which scenario. People default to Kernel or Functional tests because the Drupal architecture and the test tooling have historically made those easiest to write, even when, in principle, a Unit test would have been faster, cheaper, and equally valid.

This session makes the case for adopting the test pyramid as an explicit, community-endorsed strategy for Drupal core, contrib, and custom code: this will require both coming up with precise guidelines and designing our code with better unit testability in mind.

Prerequisites: Have written at least one PHPUnit test in a Drupal context (any type); familiar with distinction between UnitTestCase, KernelTestBase, and BrowserTestBase; basic understanding of mocking concepts.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: Next Generation ECA - Vision and Progress update
schedule.desc:
This session details the future roadmap for ECA, aiming to broaden its accessibility and impact within the Drupal community by making it usable for all users, regardless of technical expertise, and expanding its capabilities beyond just developers and site builders.

ECA (the Event, Condition, Action module) for modern Drupal has established itself as a no-code/low-code workflow automation tool. The next generation aims to achieve these goals:

  • Expand usage from current 1% to all Drupal users, including those with minimal platform experience
  • Enable users to achieve success with ECA within minutes through an intuitive interface
  • Guide users in elevating their skills as they progress
  • Extend beyond developers and site builders to enable all users to build workflows and automations

The session outlines how maintainers and the community plan to achieve these goals and progress made to date.

Experience Level: Anyone

schedule.title: One Brand Voice from 35 Sources: How We Rebuilt VisitEurope.com and How Drupal AI Unifies Its Tone
schedule.desc:
How do you unify 35 distinct national voices into one cohesive European travel brand? Discover how Brainsum combined content strategy, Drupal's robust architecture, and generative AI to transform VisitEurope.com from a legacy site into a lightning-fast, unified editorial platform.

Challenge: VisitEurope.com, managed by the European Travel Commission (ETC) with 35 national tourism organisations, suffered from poor mobile responsiveness, 600+ redundant interest tags, and load times exceeding 10 seconds while managing 2000+ pages from heterogeneous sources.

Solution: Comprehensive content strategy analysis defined tone of voice and editorial principles. Drupal AI now aligns incoming content from all 35 sources to match the VisitEurope brand voice before publication.

Results: Load times dropped from over 10 seconds to under 200ms; zero pages now fail Core Web Vitals.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: Client Experience is Everyone’s Responsibility
schedule.desc:
Client Experience is at the heart of everything we do in the agency world but we often silo the responsibility of just a few, specific team members. How do you make everyone in your agency a Client Experience expert? Enter: Client Experience Academy (CXA) an internal training program that goes beyond technical skills to build the professional competencies that make client relationships thrive.

This session will take you behind the scenes of creating, implementing, and iterating on a structured professional development program. You'll learn how we designed content that bridges the gap between internal team dynamics and external client success, the challenges we faced running it with both producers/project managers and engineers, and the measurable impacts on our client relationships and team culture.

Experience Level: Anyone

schedule.title: Drupal AI Product Update: From Foundation to Agentic Workflows
schedule.desc:
Join the Product Managers of the Drupal AI Initiative for the official update on Drupal's transformation into a production-ready Agentic CMS. Discover how the latest suite of AI Recipes, robust guardrails, and automated content reviews allow you to safely deploy advanced AI workflows in minutes.

Drupal has made a massive commitment to AI, backed by over 30 leading ecosystem companies, and the foundational architecture is now ready. Over the last year, the Drupal AI Initiative has built the core governance and abstractions that make a production-ready, agentic infrastructure possible.

The presentation will dive deep into the new ecosystem of AI Recipes, the robust governance layer (AI Guardrails, AI Observability, Context Control Center), and live demonstrations of AI Content Reviews, semantic search capabilities, and embedded AI assistants.

Prerequisites: A basic understanding of Drupal site building and a general familiarity with AI/LLM concepts. No advanced AI engineering or Python experience is required.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: From Chatbots to AI Experiences: The Next Evolution of the Website
schedule.desc:
Your website isn't dead, but it's evolving. Instead of static pages and navigation, visitors are beginning to interact with websites conversationally. The next generation of digital experiences will combine AI assistants, real-time personalization, and dynamic page assembly to guide users through complete journeys rather than just deliver information.

Websites are entering a new phase where visitors no longer just browse pages but expect to interact conversationally and receive immediate responses. Early AI implementations focused on chatbots or AI-powered search, but these only scratch the surface of what AI can enable.

This session explores how digital assistants on websites are evolving into an experience layer capable of assembling personalized journeys. Instead of just answering questions, they guide visitors through actions, surface relevant content, trigger forms or widgets, and reshape the page experience based on user input.

  • The evolution from chatbots and AI search to AI-driven web experiences
  • How conversation drives real-time personalization on websites
  • Forms, widgets, CTAs, and guided journeys within an assistant experience
  • Digital assistants interacting with CMS content, APIs, and enterprise systems

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: From Passion to Pressure: Rethinking Sustainability in Open Source Communities
schedule.desc:
Building and sustaining communities presents distinct challenges. Over years of organizing Drupal meetups, camps, and contributing to DrupalCon, the presenter has experienced both the energy and pressure inherent in community work. What appears vibrant externally often relies on a small number of individuals consistently participating and maintaining momentum.

While community revival and growth were once primary focuses, maintaining that momentum has introduced new obstacles. This session offers candid insights into community organizing realities, including pressure to sustain engagement, difficulties with shared accountability, and moments of overwhelming responsibility.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: Page Builder Deathmatch: Canvas vs Display Builder in a Real World Project
schedule.desc:
"Canvas or Display Builder? Which one is the right tool for your job? And what may explode if you install both?"

Two contenders. One Drupal site. An incorrect choice for your task can consume days or weeks. Canvas and Display Builder are both nearing production maturity and promise to transform how editors, site builders, and designers engage with Drupal. However, they rest on fundamentally different assumptions, making the selection between them a critical architectural decision.

This session evaluates both tools across three rounds: Page Layout (can they replace Drupal's fragmented theming approach?), Managing Displays (how do they handle Drupal's data model and component mapping?), and Frontpage Gauntlet (flexible landing pages requiring editorial autonomy, multilingual content, media handling, and AI workflows).

Each round uses real project requirements. Gotchas, workarounds, and limitations are identified. The session concludes with a practical decision framework.

Prerequisites: Basic familiarity with Drupal's content model; knowledge of Drupal's theming or layout system (SDCs, layout builder, paragraphs, or block layout); experiences with other page builders.

Experience Level: Anyone

schedule.title: Skin in the game: Digital Sovereignty, AI and Sustainability in Drupal
schedule.desc:
As AI adoption accelerates and SaaS platforms dominate the digital landscape, organisations—especially in the public sector—face a critical question: who controls their digital future? This interactive workshop explores digital sovereignty in the context of Drupal, AI, and sustainable web governance, drawing on real-world experience from the University of Edinburgh's EdWeb2 platform and the Edinburgh Language Model (ELM).

Digital platforms function as strategic assets, yet many organisations depend increasingly on external SaaS providers and opaque AI systems. This workshop will:

  • Introduce digital sovereignty concepts in a Drupal context
  • Explore risks and trade-offs of AI adoption, including data privacy, vendor lock-in, and governance
  • Examine how platform strategy can reduce duplication and improve sustainability
  • Discuss environmental and organisational dimensions of sustainable digital ecosystems

Interactive Activities: Participants work in small groups on scenario exercises, sovereignty mapping, and architecture sketching, then share insights and reflect on trade-offs.

Experience Level: Anyone

schedule.title: How can we improve Drupal's visibility in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude?
schedule.desc:
More and more people are using AI systems, esp. LLMs, to learn about technologies, compare options, and decide what to use. So how Drupal shows up in those answers matters.

This BoF is about a simple question: what can each of us do to help AI systems understand and represent Drupal better?

We will talk about things the Drupal community already creates every day, such as documentation, blog posts, case studies, discussions, and answers to common questions, and how these may influence what artificial intelligence tools know about Drupal.

Some of the questions we will discuss:

  • Where does Drupal show up well today, and where could it be better?
  • What kind of content helps AI systems understand what Drupal is, what it is good at, and where it fits?
  • What can individual community members do through the work they are already doing?
  • Which gaps in Drupal content are worth filling?
  • Are there things we could do together as a community to improve how Drupal is represented?

You don't need any experience with AI search to join. We want to hear different perspectives, whether you work with Drupal every day, contribute occasionally, or are simply curious about the topic. This is an open community discussion, and every point of view is welcome.

schedule.title: Applying Web Sustainability Guidelines to Drupal Projects: From Design to Refactoring
schedule.desc:
Digital sustainability is becoming a key responsibility for organisations building and operating web platforms. The environmental impact of websites—through infrastructure usage, inefficient code, and heavy interfaces—directly affects the long-term health of the open web, particularly for public sector and large-scale platforms.

The Web Sustainability Guidelines (WSG) provide a comprehensive framework, but applying them in real Drupal projects is not always straightforward. This session presents a practical, step-by-step approach to integrating WSG into Drupal 10/11 projects: from design and development to deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement.

  • Design: reducing complexity and optimising media
  • Development & deployment: efficient configuration and caching
  • Monitoring: measuring performance and impact
  • Refactoring: prioritising improvements over time

Examples from real Drupal projects will be shared, showing how optimising assets and cache efficiency reduced page weight, lowered estimated carbon emissions, and improved performance.

Prerequisites: Basic understanding of Drupal (site building or development) and general web performance concepts such as caching and frontend optimisation. No prior knowledge of sustainability frameworks is required.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: From Overwhelm to Opportunity: Designing a Personalised Career Journey for 350+ NHS Roles
schedule.desc:
How do you help someone choose a career when you offer 350 options? This talk shows how we turned overwhelming NHS career data into a guided, personalised journey, using Drupal to model complexity and design for uncertainty.

NHS Health Careers serves one of the UK's most diverse digital audiences, from a 14-year-old picking GCSEs to a clinician pivoting careers. With 350+ roles, 1,000+ courses, and five legacy sites being merged into one, the challenge was designing a system to help people answer: "What should I do with my life?"

This session covers how complex content relationships enabled personalisation, guided discovery tools replaced overwhelming choice with intentional journeys, and an external career-matching quiz API was integrated for both anonymous and authenticated users.

The result includes a personalised careers hub with a gamified career planner, contextual content filtering, and an adaptive homepage.

Experience Level: Beginner

schedule.title: The Reality of Accessibility Automation
schedule.desc:
Accessibility automation is often viewed as a complete solution for inclusive digital products. With tools like axe, Lighthouse, and CI-integrated scanners becoming standard, many teams assume automated testing ensures compliance. However, the reality is considerably more nuanced.

This session explores the genuine capabilities and limitations of accessibility automation. It examines what automated tools reliably detect, where they fall short, and why significant portions of WCAG success criteria require human evaluation. Through practical examples, the speaker highlights the gap between rule-based validation and actual user experience—particularly for screen reader users, keyboard-only users, and people with cognitive disabilities.

The session also considers AI's emerging role in accessibility testing: how it might bridge semantic and contextual gaps that traditional automation cannot address, where it provides value, and where limitations remain.

Prerequisites: None; content explained from foundational level.

Experience Level: Beginner
