schedule.title: 163 → 42: Dismantling and Reassembling a Drupal Migration with AI
schedule.desc:
What happens when your migration source has 163 paragraph types — some containing entire pages of mixed HTML in a single field — and your destination architecture has 42 typed paragraph bundles? This presentation explores a transformation problem that reimagines how migrations can work.

Instead of traditional one-to-one mapping, the approach involves: deeply understanding source data with AI-assisted analysis, decomposing monolithic content into typed fragments, and deriving/assembling destination content from multiple source streams.

The methodology was applied to a large Drupal 10 to Drupal 11 website migration, making AI a first-class participant for source data analysis at scale. An AI agent with 12 atomic skills (database discovery, orphan detection, field population measurement, cross-reference tracing) transformed source analysis into a repeatable capability accessible from the first sprint.

Prerequisites: Basic understanding of Drupal's Migrate API (source, process, destination plugins); familiarity with paragraph-based content architectures; general awareness of AI agents and LLM-based tools.

Experience Level: Intermediate

schedule.title: AI Mid-Life Crisis: failure stories from the silent majority
schedule.desc:
The session addresses the psychological barriers developers face when adopting AI tools. Rather than focusing on prompt engineering techniques, it presents an honest examination of real-world AI failures within Drupal development contexts. The speakers highlight that while polished demonstrations showcase AI's capabilities, practical applications often produce a "hallucinated mess of Drupal 7 hooks and broken YAMLs."

The discussion explores why many developers feel discouraged by the rapid pace of AI advancement and the gap between expert practitioners and those beginning their journey. It emphasizes normalizing struggles and moving beyond the "10x developer myth."

Learning objectives:

  • Normalize the struggle: remove psychological barriers preventing experimentation
  • The anatomy of an AI fail: examine specific LLM limitations with Drupal complexity
  • Building a failure library: enable teams to share and learn from AI failures collaboratively

Prerequisites: None. Experience level: Beginner. Target audience: Developers wanting to learn AI tools but discouraged by rapid changes.

schedule.title: Drupal Canvas Code Components: Modern JavaScript, agentic engineering, and the road ahead
schedule.desc:
Modern JavaScript combined with agentic engineering integrates with Drupal through Drupal Canvas Code Components. The session explores current capabilities and future directions for this technology.

Web UI development in 2026 relies heavily on JavaScript, supported by a robust open-source ecosystem. Drupal Canvas accommodates both Twig-based Single-Directory Components and JavaScript/React-based Code Components, managed independently without requiring Drupal expertise.

Code Components debuted at DrupalCon Atlanta with an integrated code editor, previews, React, and Tailwind CSS support. Drupal CMS 2 includes Canvas by default. The evolution progressed from browser-based instant iterations to a CLI tool enabling local codebase synchronization. The latest phase fully leverages the JavaScript ecosystem and AI coding agents, expanding capabilities to pages, content templates, and global regions. Canvas Workbench provides local preview functionality.

Learning objectives: Attendees will understand the future direction of Code Components in Drupal Canvas and how to integrate capabilities into standard JavaScript codebases utilizing agentic tooling.

Prerequisite: Familiarity with modern JavaScript UI framework codebases. Target audience: Frontend engineers considering React-based UI components for Drupal Canvas. Experience level: Intermediate.

schedule.title: First-Time Contributor Workshop - Wednesday
Scolta: Drop-in AI Search Without a Search Server
schedule.desc:
"What if you could replace Solr with something that runs in the browser, costs almost nothing, and delivers better results?" This session introduces Scolta, an open-source search toolkit combining client-side search via Pagefind with an AI layer for query expansion and summaries. The architecture uses a shared Rust/WebAssembly core with a PHP bridge supporting Drupal, Laravel, and WordPress. Search executes entirely in the browser with no backend server required. AI features layer on top, handling query expansion, result summarization, and conversational followups. A live demonstration is included.

Prerequisite: Familiarity with Drupal's search landscape (core search, Search API, Solr) is helpful but not required. No Rust or WebAssembly experience needed.

Target audience: Developers, site builders, and technical leads evaluating search solutions for Drupal sites. Also relevant for anyone managing search infrastructure costs or navigating GDPR/data sovereignty requirements.

Learning objectives:

  • Evaluate whether client-side search is a viable replacement for Solr, Elasticsearch, or SaaS search on Drupal sites
  • Understand the Scolta architecture and how a shared Rust/WASM core serves multiple CMS platforms
  • Make informed decisions about adding AI search features, considering cost, data sovereignty, and model selection

Experience level: Intermediate.

schedule.title: SDCs, Canvas, and the Agent That Builds With Them
schedule.desc:
This session explores an AI-driven page-building workflow centered on Single-Directory Components (SDCs) and Drupal Canvas. The presenter demonstrates how an AI agent can generate, deploy, and verify components within a Drupal environment, bridging the gap between natural language requests and production-ready code.

The discussion covers why SDCs' predictable structure makes them ideal for AI generation, how Model Context Protocol (MCP) tooling grants agents content management capabilities, and how browser automation validates rendered output. A live demonstration shows the complete workflow, including where human oversight remains critical.

Prerequisites:

  • Familiarity with Drupal theme development
  • Working knowledge of SDCs (structure, YAML schema, Twig templates)
  • Basic comfort with CLI tools; no prior AI agent experience required

Learning objectives:

  • Generate production-ready SDC bundles using AI agent skills tuned for Drupal
  • Understand MCP tooling for agent access to Drupal's page management layer
  • Apply browser automation to verify rendered output during component development
  • Identify where human judgment remains essential in agent-assisted workflows

Target audience: Drupal theme and front-end developers. Experience level: Anyone.

schedule.title: Super charging SDC design systems with Web Components
schedule.desc:
"The age of React.js is over. Web Components have arrived." Learn practical tips to building or reusing design systems with Web Component APIs and SDC.

This session explores how browser-native Web Components now support server-side rendering across all major browsers as of August 2026. Participants will learn how to leverage Drupal's Single Directory Components (SDC) to build performant design systems using vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS without requiring additional frameworks or bundlers.

Learning objectives:

  • Briefly review the three APIs of Web Components: Custom Elements, Templates and Slots, Shadow DOM
  • Discuss the accessibility issues with Shadow DOM
  • Compare components with declarative Shadow DOM vs Light DOM
  • Techniques for using SDC to build Light DOM and Shadow DOM web components

Prerequisite: Developers should be familiar with SDC and JavaScript; expert knowledge is not required. Target audience: Frontend developers and designers. Experience level: Intermediate.

schedule.title: AI Assists, Humans Decide: Agentic Workflows in Drupal - A Drupal AI Hackathon Story
schedule.desc:
Content editors at the European Commission manage hundreds of websites across 24 languages, facing challenges in accuracy, readability, policy compliance, and consistency at scale. During the EC's Drupal AI Hackathon in January 2026, a team developed an AI-powered content validation engine that won first place. This session demonstrates the solution and explores the architectural decisions behind it.

The system enables editors to validate, improve, and monitor content throughout its lifecycle using AI that evaluates content against configurable editorial rules covering fact accuracy, readability, SEO, and policy alignment. Crucially, "AI assists and humans stay in control" — the assistant operates in an isolated environment where editors review suggestions before any changes affect published content, with every modification requiring explicit human approval.

The presentation covers why Drupal was chosen to orchestrate AI steps rather than delegating to an LLM agent, async execution, vendor-independent model integration, and data sovereignty strategies.

Prerequisites:

  • General knowledge of Drupal site building and content editing
  • Basic concepts of AI and Agentic AI
  • Familiarity with entities, forms, or APIs
  • No prior AI experience required

Target audience: Agency leaders, solution architects, innovation teams, technical strategists.

Learning objectives:

  • Architect agentic AI workflows where Drupal orchestrates processes and LLMs execute discrete steps, understanding implications for cost, speed, and reliability
  • Apply human-in-the-loop design enforced deterministically rather than through AI prompting
  • Combine rule-based checks with contextual AI evaluation, deploying each optimally
  • Implement data sovereignty strategies within agentic workflows

Experience level: Intermediate.

schedule.title: AI-Powered Site Building in Drupal: From Blank Site to Styled Pages in a Conversation
schedule.desc:
This session demonstrates how non-technical users can build complete Drupal sites through natural-language conversation with AI. The presentation opens with a live demo showing site creation from a blank installation, including homepage, about page, taxonomy-driven blog listing, navigation menu, styled footer, and AI-generated images, refined through contextual chat.

The technical architecture employs a discovery-first approach using function-call tools that allow AI to introspect component schemas, layouts, design tokens, and site structure. The workflow covers AI-proposed structure validation, self-correction loops, context-aware editing, asynchronous image generation, and persistent conversational memory across sessions.

Styling is managed through a per-component CSS cascade across four levels: global tokens, component defaults, per-page overrides, and per-instance styles. The session concludes with discussion of provider portability via the contrib AI module and editorial governance through Workspaces Extra.

Learning objectives: Attendees will understand architectural patterns for reliable conversational page-building systems; designing per-component styling cascades aligned with design systems; using Workspaces Extra for editorial governance of AI-generated content; adapting this approach across various page builders; and realistic assessment of when AI-assisted building adds value.

Prerequisites: Familiarity with Drupal's editorial interface, content architecture (content types, blocks, menus, taxonomy), and general awareness of LLM tool-calling concepts. Experience level: Intermediate. Target audience: Drupal developers or technical architects building component-driven sites.

schedule.title: Building for Drupal Canvas: Lessons Learned from Real-World Use
schedule.desc:
Drupal Canvas represents a significant transformation in how Drupal sites are constructed, providing editors with greater autonomy and creative control. However, developing components that function effectively within this new environment demands an adjusted development approach.

This presentation explores hands-on insights from creating components optimized for Drupal Canvas. Attendees will discover proven strategies, common pitfalls, and techniques for building systems that work well for both development teams and content creators.

Key topics include: creating interfaces that streamline editor workflows; applying contemporary CSS system methodologies to construct adaptable components; designing flexible layouts with uniform spacing; working with global regions and templates; managing images within Canvas; establishing appropriate component organization; optimizing for performance and AI-powered content generation; and recognizing Canvas's current strengths and constraints.

The session also addresses future directions for Drupal Canvas and approaches for ensuring component longevity as the ecosystem develops.

Ideal for frontend developers, themers, and those constructing design systems in Drupal. Experience level: Intermediate.

schedule.title: From Drupal Content to AI Answers: Learnings from EPSY
schedule.desc:
EPSY, the European Personnel Selection Office's AI assistant, demonstrates an alternative approach to traditional chatbots. Rather than conversational interaction, it functions as a constrained AI search interface purpose-built for public sector environments.

This session examines how EPSY guides tens of thousands of recruitment candidates through intricate, multilingual workflows while maintaining compliance and user trust. The presentation analyzes design decisions including prompting strategies, strict query framing, and controlled outputs.

Key topics span the distinction between chat and search UX, prioritizing accuracy over fluency, and deploying AI within regulated contexts. Attendees will gain practical patterns for implementing AI-assisted search functionality within Drupal projects.

Prerequisites:

  • Basic understanding of Drupal content architecture
  • Familiarity with search concepts (Solr, Elasticsearch, or similar)
  • General awareness of LLMs

Target audience: Drupal site builders, webmasters, content managers, and developers using Drupal as a CMS for public or private sector websites. Particularly relevant for professionals exploring AI integration into existing digital ecosystems.

Learning objectives:

  • Understand differences between chat UX and AI search UX
  • Learn how EPSY reduces hallucination risk through design
  • Identify when to use stateless versus conversational AI
  • Map RAG patterns to Drupal architectures
  • Apply guardrails for AI in regulated environments

Experience level: Intermediate.

schedule.title: From SEO to GEO: What Changes, What Doesn’t
schedule.desc:
"AI-powered search is taking over... or is it? Is SEO really dead? Do we need a whole new playbook?" This session explores Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) by separating fact from hype. Drawing on extensive hands-on experience, the presenter distinguishes between misconceptions and reality regarding the shift from traditional search engines to AI-driven answer engines.

The discussion covers the biggest misunderstandings about GEO, where AI search genuinely affects visibility and traffic, and why technical foundations and quality content remain critical. Attendees will explore the substantial overlap between SEO and GEO, along with practical modifications worth implementing.

Rather than chasing acronyms, this talk provides clarity for navigating AI-powered search confidently, emphasizing that GEO represents an evolution of SEO, not a replacement.

Learning objectives: Attendees will be able to differentiate between traditional SEO and GEO to prioritize marketing efforts, identify which site strategies are "AI-proof," implement practical content and technical adjustments for both search types, and communicate a hype-free search evolution strategy to stakeholders.

Prerequisites: Basic understanding of search engine functionality and familiarity with Large Language Models; basic SEO knowledge helpful but not required. Target audience: Primary — marketers, webmasters; secondary — developers. Experience level: Intermediate.

schedule.title: Getting the most out of Editoria11y v3
schedule.desc:
Drupal CMS's accessibility recipe "just works" most of the time. When seeking improved performance, site administrators discover more than 130 configuration fields distributed across three settings tabs. This session explores how the project evolved to this point and provides actionable guidance on setup and customization.

Learning objectives:

  • Learn to fine-tune your accessibility checker for theme-specific and editor-specific issues
  • Discover documentation and code examples for extending the checker
  • Feel confident navigating 130+ configuration fields across three tabs

Prerequisites: None. Target audience: Quality assurance professionals, including site owners, QA managers, and developers focused on enhancing the editing experience. Experience level: Anyone.

schedule.title: Reinventing the Editorial Experience: How Mars Innovated with Drupal Canvas at Enterprise Scale
schedule.desc:
Mars, a globally recognized consumer brand operating over 350 Drupal websites, sought to empower non-technical stakeholders — marketers, creative agencies, and brand teams — to manage digital content independently. Rather than replacing their mature Drupal foundation, they invested in Drupal Canvas, a component-based platform designed to democratize access to web content management.

The presentation explores Mars's strategic decision to innovate atop existing infrastructure and examines how Drupal Canvas architecture supports global, multi-brand operations. Speakers will discuss the enhanced editorial experience for non-technical users, governance frameworks, change management strategies, and practical lessons learned throughout implementation.

Learning objectives:

  • Understand why an established Drupal organization chose Drupal Canvas investment
  • Explain how Drupal Canvas enables independent work for non-technical users
  • Identify architectural and governance decisions enabling enterprise-scale multisite platforms
  • Apply Mars's experience to personal editorial workflows and platform strategy

Prerequisites: No deep technical knowledge required; basic CMS familiarity and understanding of multisite platforms beneficial. Experience level: Beginner. Target audience: Digital leaders, CMOs, product owners, agency leaders.

schedule.title: From local voices to global impact: Powering World Cancer Day with Drupal and AI
schedule.desc:
Each year, World Cancer Day mobilizes global participation with communities activating worldwide, hundreds of personal stories shared in over 60 languages, and traffic surges to more than 500,000 requests per hour. The presentation explores how UICC leverages Drupal as the foundational platform for this campaign, maintaining resilience and inclusivity during peak demand while integrating AI to streamline moderation and content publishing without displacing human storytellers.

The session covers five strategic areas: global user-generated content visibility through real-time mapping, AI-powered storytelling via Azure-based systems, multilingual content management across 60+ languages, infrastructure optimization using Fastly CDN and predictive scaling, and innovative campaign features including custom poster generators.

Prerequisite: Interest in digital strategy, global campaign management, or high-traffic architecture. Deep technical expertise not required, though familiarity with AI and CMS scalability beneficial.

Target audience: Product owners, digital strategists, marketing managers, NGO leaders, project managers, and architects interested in scaling impact and AI integration.

Learning objectives:

  • Prepare for high-traffic events without year-round infrastructure costs
  • Implement responsible AI for sensitive, high-volume content moderation
  • Support 60+ languages within manageable editorial workflows
  • Understand Drupal's strategic ROI for global organizations

Experience level: Anyone.

schedule.title: How Marketers Win in an AI‑First Search World (AEO & GEO Playbook)
schedule.desc:
Organic traffic declines despite solid SEO fundamentals because search behavior has fundamentally shifted. AI Overviews, conversational search, and LLM-driven discovery now serve as the initial touchpoint in user journeys, often providing answers before users click traditional results.

This session addresses why conventional analytics misrepresent performance and how AI systems determine content citations. Drawing from optimization work across 180+ global websites for UNICEF, speakers present a practical AEO/GEO framework enabling marketing teams and agencies to transition from keyword ranking to earning citations and trust within AI ecosystems.

The approach offers an actionable operating model for acquiring customers through AI-powered discovery channels.

Prerequisites: Basic understanding of SEO and content marketing fundamentals; familiarity with Google Analytics and Google Search Console; experience managing or influencing website content, structure, or strategy.

Learning objectives: Participants will be able to explain organic traffic declines despite strong SEO practices; understand how AI systems evaluate and cite content; distinguish between keyword ranking and AI citations; apply proven AEO/GEO frameworks to existing websites; align teams around AI-era discovery; and shift success metrics from clicks to authority and intent.

Experience level: Intermediate.

schedule.title: How we made the biggest performance gains in a decade in Drupal core
schedule.desc:
Drupal 11.4 achieved approximately 50% reductions in database queries and cache I/O compared to Drupal 11.0, alongside various front-end performance enhancements. This presentation explores the technical approaches that enabled these improvements and provides guidance for implementing similar optimization strategies on your own projects.

A thorough exploration of recent performance advancements within Drupal core will be presented, focusing on dynamic page cache refinements and Fibers technology.

Prerequisites: Either substantial expertise in web performance and application monitoring, or deep knowledge of Drupal development. Target audience: Technical professionals.

Learning objectives: Participants should develop improved comprehension of Drupal's caching, rendering infrastructure, and related systems. Additional takeaways include practical approaches for applying performance testing and profiling tools like xhprof to contributed modules or client implementations.

Experience level: Advanced.

schedule.title: Modern Video in Drupal: AV1, Responsive Sources, CDN Providers, and a Better Contrib Architecture
schedule.desc:
The session addresses a significant gap in Drupal's capabilities. While image handling has matured considerably, video delivery remains underdeveloped in the core platform and fragmented across contributed modules. This presentation explores how modern architecture — leveraging AV1 codec support, responsive source selection, provider plugins, and production-tested patterns — can advance Drupal's video ecosystem.

The speaker presents three standalone contrib modules designed to work independently or in concert, mirroring how image styles function for images. Coverage includes native video rendering versus iframe-based approaches, integration with external media and CDN providers, responsive mapping strategies, caching considerations, and fallback mechanisms.

Learning objectives:

  1. Identify current limitations in Drupal core and contrib video solutions for contemporary delivery requirements
  2. Compare architectural approaches for Drupal video implementation, including native rendering, responsive sources, provider abstractions, and fallback tactics
  3. Design and evaluate sustainable Drupal 11 video strategies compatible with modern codecs and external delivery systems
  4. Weigh the merits of in-platform video handling against outsourcing encoding and delivery to specialized providers

Prerequisites: Attendees should possess comfort with Drupal site building and foundational knowledge of media entities and field formatters. Developer familiarity with Drupal 10/11, PHP, and contrib module architecture is beneficial but not required; the session maintains practical accessibility for advanced site builders and technical leads.

Experience level: Intermediate.

schedule.title: Okay, Houston, we've had a problem here — Wiring Drupal into a Full-Scale Agentic Operations Platform
schedule.desc:
An agency built Houston, an AI operations platform in Rust that positions Drupal at the center of a multi-system ecosystem. Through MCP servers and CLI tools, an AI assistant can create Drupal content, manage project tasks, triage support tickets, generate invoices, search emails, and control smart home devices from a single message.

The platform closes feedback loops between ticketing systems and code generation. When an OpenProject ticket requests a new content type or module, Houston reads the specification, creates a feature branch, writes code against the existing codebase, and opens a merge request with confidence scoring.

The core infrastructure includes a scheduler managing 50+ tasks, vector memory for security, a learning engine, and a real-time voice pipeline supporting German and English. The session demonstrates GDPR-compliant deployment using EU models and local inference on Apple Silicon.

Learning objectives:

  1. How to expose a Drupal site as an MCP server and its current AI agent capabilities
  2. Production architecture for orchestrating Drupal with 10+ systems using MCP servers and a Rust core engine
  3. How voice interfaces and semantic memory transform chatbots into operations platforms
  4. GDPR-compliant AI deployment strategies with EU-hosted and local models
  5. The boundary between community contribution and commercial products within the Drupal ecosystem

Prerequisites: Comfortable with Drupal development (module installation, configuration, basic architecture). Familiarity with APIs and command-line tools is helpful. No AI/ML background required. Target audience: Developers, technical leads, and agency CTOs. Experience level: Anyone.

schedule.title: Supply Chain Security in Drupal and Composer
schedule.desc:
This session examines the Drupal Association's efforts to strengthen Drupal sites against emerging threats. The presentation begins with an overview of software supply chain vulnerabilities, then explores the Auto-Updates Initiative, which provides smaller site operators with streamlined update tools. Attendees will learn about The Update Framework (TUF) and its protocols for ensuring package integrity, followed by demonstrations of the Rugged TUF Server and Composer TUF plugin designed to protect the Drupal community.

Prerequisites:

  • Familiarity with how Composer is used to install package dependencies
  • Basic understanding of deployment processes
  • Basic understanding of web application security fundamentals
  • Knowledge of Drupal deployment and update best practices (beneficial)

Target audience: Drupal developers, site administrators, security professionals, PHP developers, DevOps engineers, technical decision-makers, and researchers interested in software supply chain security.

Learning objectives:

  • Better understand the threats of software supply chain attacks
  • Learn best practices for securing Drupal sites against supply chain attacks
  • Learn how the Drupal Association has built solutions protecting the entire Drupal community

Experience level: Intermediate.
